triage.verifier_justification: The §122 rule's proof atoms — unchanged by this commit — ground versions[1].formula on the 9903.03.03 "(aa)(ii) exclusion list" and on "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04", yet the pre-fix branch zeroed the 10% surcharge on `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, flags the same diff renames to `entry_is_china_301_list123` and `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` elsewhere in the file, i.e. §301-list and aluminum-list membership, which the §122 source nowhere makes exempting. Heading resolution at the pinned release confirms the structure: 9903.03.01 imposes "+ 10%" on all articles "Except for products described in headings 9903.03.02–9903.03.11", and 9903.03.03 carries the note 2(aa)(ii) exclusion; the fix re-grounds the gate on `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered`. I tried to refute this as a pure "generalize" refactor and could not: the PR treats the old behavior as wrong law, and the witness-slice gate enumerates value-changing cells "where the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part". untraceable_branch (a condition with no basis in the cited source, re-grounded) fits better than wrong_entity_or_scope, polarity_or_logic, or unrepresented_clause.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts and what survived: (1) "mechanical / generator bump only" fails — formula tokens change in five component rules and a new rule (`section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch99a_s232_steel_heading_rate`) is added and wired into `schedule_statutory_stack`. (2) "not_a_defect, new coverage the module never claimed" fails — the §122 component already produced values for every ch99a line; the PR's witness-slice gate explicitly accepts changed cells as the class "where the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part", i.e. the old outputs are asserted wrong. (3) "wrong_entity_or_scope" is the nearest competitor (wrong population of lines exempted), but entity/period/dtype/output are unchanged; the wrongness is the grounding of the branch condition, which the taxonomy assigns to untraceable_branch. Caveats for the reviewer: (a) the commit carries several defects of the same family — `brazil_section_301_component_rate` and `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` lose the same `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0` gate and gain listed-line conditions, and the new steel component is arguably unrepresented_clause — so if the corpus dedupes per commit rather than per rule_path, this case should stay anchored to rules[section_122_component_rate].versions[1].formula; (b) provenance wrinkle unrelated to the verdict: under the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS 2026 Rev. 3) the §122 exception atoms' page anchors do not resolve to their quoted excerpts — `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221` returns note subdivisions (x)–(z) and `page-230` returns §232 steel notes with no "9903.82.02" string; heading-level paths `us/statute/hts/9903.03.01` and `.03` do resolve and confirm the exclusion structure, and the module elsewhere states it uses a Rev. 15 vintage, so the page drift is likely a revision mismatch rather than a fabricated citation.
